'''Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace''' (''née'' Byron; 10 December 1815 –
27 November 1852) was an English [[mathematician]] and writer, chiefly known
for her work on Charles Babbage's proposed [[mechanical computer|mechanical
general-purpose computer]], the [[Analytical Engine]].<ref name="bio">Toole,
Betty A. (1998). ''Ada, the Enchantress of Numbers''. p.&nbsp;12.</ref>

== Biography ==
She was the only legitimate child of the poet Lord [[Byron]] and his wife
[[Anne Isabella Byron|Lady Byron]].{{sfn|Turney|1972|p=35}} All her
half-siblings were born out of wedlock.

=== Early life ===
Ada described her approach as "poetical science"<ref>See {{harvnb|Woolley|1999}}.</ref>
and herself as an "Analyst (& Metaphysician)".

She was often visited by [https://example.org/scientists notable scientists],
including {{nowrap|Charles Babbage}} and Michael Faraday.
